subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A(5,3) and B(3,−2) are two fixed points. Find the equation of locus of P, so that the area of triangle PAB is 9 sq.units.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name the area formula you would use, and say how many lines the locus turns out to be.

steps.label: Take the locus point
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. A and B are the fixed ends of the base; P is the vertex that moves.
steps.memory_tip: A and B are fixed; P is the moving vertex.
lines: Let P = (x, y) be a point on the locus.

recall.must_convey: That the moving point is named P = (x, y) and the fixed points are written down.
accept: let P be x comma y
take the locus point as P x y
P equals x comma y is on the locus
locus point ni P x y ga teesukovali
name the moving point P with coordinates x and y

steps.why: Every locus question starts the same way: the moving point gets coordinates, and the condition is then written in terms of those coordinates.
common_mistakes: Giving the moving point fixed numbers instead of (x, y).
Mixing up which points are fixed and which one moves.

steps.label: Write the given condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. The area of a triangle from three coordinate pairs is the half-determinant form. Writing it with the given area on the right earns the mark.
steps.memory_tip: The half-determinant area form, with the given 9 on the right.

recall.must_convey: That the area is written as one half of the 2x2 determinant of coordinate differences, set equal to the given area.
accept: area is half the determinant of the coordinate differences
use the half mod determinant formula for the area of a triangle
write delta equals half determinant equals the given area
area formula half determinant vaadali
half into the determinant of x one minus x two and so on

steps.why: Area is the one condition in this chapter that needs a determinant rather than a distance, and the half-determinant form is the one the board expects.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the factor ½ in front of the determinant.
Dropping the modulus bars, which decides whether both branches survive.

steps.label: Substitute the coordinates
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The determinant rows are differences of coordinates, so the moving point (x, y) enters as the third pair. Expand the 2×2 determinant as a cross product of diagonals.
steps.memory_tip: Expand the 2×2 determinant as a cross product of its diagonals.

recall.must_convey: That the given coordinates and (x, y) go into the determinant, which is then expanded to a modulus of a linear expression.
accept: put the coordinates into the determinant and expand it
substitute A B and the moving point then open the two by two determinant
expand the determinant as the difference of the diagonal products
coordinates substitute chesi determinant expand cheyyali
the determinant becomes a modulus of a linear expression

steps.why: Once the numbers are in, the determinant is a single 2×2 expansion and the whole condition collapses to one modulus of a linear expression.
common_mistakes: Ordering the rows so the differences come out with the wrong sign.
Expanding the determinant as a sum of diagonals instead of a difference.

steps.label: Simplify to the locus
steps.margin_note: The last two marks, and the place this family differs from every other in the chapter. A modulus opens to PLUS OR MINUS, so there are TWO lines, and both are part of the locus. Write them as one product equal to zero.
steps.memory_tip: The modulus gives ±, so the locus is TWO lines, written as one product.

recall.must_convey: That the modulus opens to plus or minus, giving TWO parallel lines, and the locus is their product equal to zero.
accept: the modulus opens to plus or minus so there are two lines and the locus is their product
remove the mod as plus or minus and multiply the two factors
there are two parallel lines, write them as a product equal to zero
mod theeste plus or minus vasthundi so rendu lines untaayi
the locus is a pair of parallel lines

steps.why: A fixed area does not pin the point to one line: it can sit on either side of AB at the same perpendicular distance, so the locus is a PAIR of parallel lines and the answer must carry both.
common_mistakes: Keeping only the + branch and reporting a single line.
Writing the two lines separately instead of as a product equal to zero.

insider_note: Double the 9 first so the determinant equals 18 and the ½ is cleared. The modulus gives ±18, so both lines survive: the answer is (5x − 2y − 37)(5x − 2y − 1) = 0, not whichever branch came out first.
